title: The long round of births
hook: the Granth speaks of many lives and the chance this human life is

segments.voice: Yesterday, karam: by deeds comes the robe, by grace the door. Your line was deeds and grace. What good deed did you do, and could you let it go without counting? Day one thousand three hundred sixty-eight.

In the evening, in homes and gurdwaras, Sikhs pray Rehras, the evening prayer. And partway through it, there's a line that sounds less like a hymn and more like a tap on the shoulder. In paraphrase: you have been given this human body; this is your turn to meet the Lord of the universe. Your turn. Like a ticket called at a counter after a long wait. The line assumes a long line, a queue of lives before this one. It doesn't argue for it. It just turns around, looks you in the eye, and says: now.
screen: `A LINE IN THE EVENING PRAYER.` → `THIS IS YOUR TURN.` → `NOW.`

segments.voice: Behind the line is the long round. The Granth speaks of the soul passing through many lives and many forms: in some hymns, as a worm, a bird, a tree, a stone, round and round. It doesn't linger on the details. The round is the background, the long road behind. Now the turn. The hymn in Rehras is by Guru Arjan, and its point is the human life. In paraphrase again: you have been given this human body; this is your turn to meet the Lord. The human life is described as the turn, the moment the door can open. Sikh teachers add that, of all the forms in the round, this is the one that can remember the Name on purpose. What is the turn for? The same hymn says, in paraphrase: your other tasks are of no use here; join the company of the holy and dwell on the Name alone. That sounds stern, but it's about priority, not about quitting work. Yesterday's farmer still farms. The line asks what the farming is for. And why does this matter on a Tuesday? If you believe in many lives, the line makes this one precious: don't waste the turn. If you don't, the line still lands: this life is the one in your hands, and today is part of it. Either way, the Guru isn't trying to frighten anyone with the long round. He's pointing at the counter where your number just came up. This life is the chance.
screen: `THE ROUND: MANY LIVES, MANY FORMS.` · `THIS HUMAN BODY: YOUR TURN.` · `OTHER TASKS WON'T DO IT.` · `TODAY IS PART OF THE TURN.` · then, large: `THIS LIFE IS THE CHANCE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: treat today as precious. Settle, and breathe. Feel your hands, your feet, the weight of your body on the seat. This body, this one. Let the thought arrive: I am here, and today is happening once. Then think of one thing you'd regret leaving undone today: a call, a moment of attention, a word of thanks. If you pray, you can offer the day as your turn. If you don't, just sit with the plain fact that you're alive right now. The bell holds the time.
The long round of births. The Granth's picture of many lives and many forms, and the human life as the turn: the chance to meet the One. Today's word.
screen: `THE LONG ROUND OF BIRTHS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: this life is the chance. Today, do the one thing you'd regret leaving undone, before the evening comes. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite Rehras Sahib in the evening, which includes Guru Arjan's line that this human body is the turn to meet the Lord of the universe.

notes: Paraphrase of 'bhaee paraapat maanukh dehureeaa, gobind milan kee ih teree bareeaa; avar kaaj terai kitai na kaam, mil saadhsangat bhaj keval naam' (Asa M5, Ang 12, in Rehras); please confirm.

The forms of the round (worm, bird, tree, stone) follow Gauri M5 'kaee janam bhae keet patangaa...' which I place at Ang 176; please confirm the Ang and that the hymn names these forms, or trim the list.
Gurmukhi ਬਰੀਆ (bareeaa, turn) taken from the Rehras line; please confirm spelling and pronunciation.
No count of lives or species is stated, deliberately.
Editor: removed 'rare' (the cited Rehras line does not say it) and attributed 'the one form that can remember the Name on purpose' to Sikh teachers; removed the First/Second/Third/Fourth template.
